Alexa Da Rosa

Compassionate, personalized counseling for individuals, couples, families, and clients working through addiction or life transitions.

Education Master of Arts in Psychology

About Alexa

Care grounded in understanding and practical support.

Alexa moved from San Diego to Mobile to pursue a Bachelor of Science degree in Psychology while playing collegiate softball at the University of Mobile. She later earned her Master of Arts degree in Psychology while serving as a full-time graduate assistant for the athletic department, completing the program at the top of her class.

Her experience includes six years working with individuals experiencing opiate and other substance addictions, leadership in a transitions program for high-risk youth in Baldwin County, and five years providing outpatient drug and alcohol and family therapy in Mobile Public Schools.

What therapy is like with Alexa

Alexa understands that no two individuals arrive in therapy with the same concerns or goals. Her approach is customized to meet each client where they are, combining warmth and collaboration with practical therapeutic strategies.

She frequently draws from Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, Motivational Interviewing, Solution-Focused Therapy, and Existential Therapy.

Back to Quiet Coast Site
Story Palette Logo Assets Voice
Quiet Coast Brand System

Care that feels rooted.

Bay Area Professional Counseling needed a visual identity that felt calm without feeling clinical, refined without feeling distant, and local without becoming decorative. The Quiet Coast direction gives the practice a warm, grounded presence that helps clients feel oriented before they read a single paragraph.

The updated identity brings together a hand-lettered coastal wordmark, a steady professional descriptor, and a small rooted botanical mark. It feels personal, established, and intentionally local.

Brand Foundation

The Quiet Coast.

The design is built around one emotional promise: you do not have to navigate it alone. Every major choice supports that idea through softness, clarity, warmth, and a sense of place.

Why this direction works

People often arrive at a counseling website carrying stress, uncertainty, grief, or the quiet hope that something could feel different. A site like this should not feel like a hospital form, a wellness trend, or a generic therapy template. It should feel like an open door.

The Quiet Coast design uses familiar Gulf Coast references to create that open-door feeling. Beach grass, oyster sand, Mobile Bay blue, marsh sage, warm paper texture, and sunset gold are not used as decoration for decoration's sake. They give the practice a sense of home. They remind clients that care can be professional and still feel human, local, and deeply welcoming.

The result is a brand that feels compassionate, rooted in place, and quietly confident. It is editorial enough to feel polished, soft enough to feel approachable, and restrained enough to keep the focus on the people seeking care.

Local Calm

The coast is referenced through tone, texture, and atmosphere, giving the practice a familiar regional identity without becoming themed or literal.

Warmth

Southern sunset colors and paper-soft neutrals replace hard clinical whites, creating a visual system that feels gentle and reassuring.

Belonging

The imagery suggests familiar places, familiar wildlife, and a sense of being held by a landscape clients may already know.

Trust

Deep Bay anchors the system with clarity and professionalism, so the brand remains credible even when the visual language is soft.

Color Palette

Drawn from coast, paper, and sunset.

The palette is intentionally quiet. Warm whites and sand tones create the canvas. Blue, sage, and deep bay tones provide regional character and structure. Sunrise Gold is held back for warmth, emphasis, and moments of optimism.

Morning Fog#F8F5F0 - main canvas
Mobile Bay Blue#689DA7 - atmosphere
Marsh Sage#A8B99A - natural support
Oyster Sand#E7DFC9 - warmth
Driftwood#6D655F - secondary text
Deep Bay#1F5963 - hierarchy
Sunrise Gold#E7B36A - quiet highlight
Logo System

Personal, polished, and easy to trust.

The updated logo works because it balances warmth and authority. The expressive wordmark gives the brand a human hand, while the professional descriptor keeps the practice clear and credible.

Why this logo was chosen

The script wordmark feels approachable and personal, which matters for counseling. It reads less like an institution and more like a steady local practice with real people behind it.

Why it works so well

The composition has enough refinement to feel established, but enough softness to lower the emotional temperature. The small rooted mark reinforces care that is grounded, compassionate, and connected to place.

Watercolor And Illustration

Familiar details, used with restraint.

The assets are designed to be felt before they are noticed. Watercolor washes soften the digital experience, while local coastal illustrations create recognition, warmth, and a sense of belonging.

Wildlife

Pelicans and egrets are familiar Gulf Coast presences. They add life and regional memory without making the site feel playful in the wrong places.

Place

Docks, shorelines, driftwood, and oyster forms quietly locate the practice near Mobile Bay. They suggest steadiness, return, and a landscape people already understand.

Home

Porches, chairs, journals, and coffee bring the brand indoors. They make the experience feel hospitable and human rather than purely clinical.

A site that sounds like a steady counselor.

The words should feel warm, clear, and quietly confident. The brand should avoid institutional language, exaggerated wellness promises, and anything that sounds like a hospital brochure. The tone is calm enough for someone in distress and refined enough for someone evaluating professional care.

Therapy language, made simpler

Therapy Approaches, Explained

Different approaches, one goal: helping you feel better, understand yourself more clearly, and move toward a life that feels meaningful.

CBT

CBT

Cognitive Behavioral Therapy

Helps you identify and change unhelpful thought patterns and behaviors so you can feel better and cope more effectively.

ACT

ACT

Acceptance & Commitment Therapy

Helps you accept difficult thoughts and feelings while taking steps toward a life that feels meaningful to you.

PC

Person-Centered Therapy

A supportive, nonjudgmental approach that puts you in the driver's seat while we focus on your growth and well-being.

SFBT

SFBT

Solution-Focused Brief Therapy

Focuses on your strengths and what's already working to help you find solutions and move toward your goals.

DBT

DBT

Dialectical Behavior Therapy

Combines acceptance and change strategies to help you manage intense emotions, build skills, and improve relationships.

MB

Mindfulness-Based Therapy

Uses mindfulness practices to help you stay present, reduce stress, and build greater awareness and compassion.

TI

Trauma-Informed Care

An approach that recognizes how trauma can affect your life and prioritizes safety, trust, choice, and empowerment.

AB

Attachment-Based Therapy

Explores how early relationships shape the way you connect with yourself and others, and how to build healthier bonds.

IFS

IFS

Internal Family Systems

Helps you understand different parts of yourself with compassion so you can heal and feel more balanced inside.

EMDR

EMDR

Eye Movement Desensitization & Reprocessing

A structured approach that helps the brain process and heal from distressing experiences.

ST

Somatic Therapy

Focuses on the connection between your body and mind to help release stress, trauma, and emotional tension.

ET

Existential Therapy

Explores life's bigger questions, like purpose, freedom, and meaning, to help you live with greater authenticity.

FS

Family Systems

Looks at how family patterns, roles, and relationships shape individual well-being and support healthier ways of relating.

CT

Couples Therapy

Supports partners in building understanding, improving communication, and creating a stronger, healthier relationship.

SB

Strengths-Based Therapy

Focuses on your unique strengths and resources to help you overcome challenges and thrive.

NT

Narrative Therapy

Looks at the stories you tell about your life and helps you rewrite them in ways that support healing and growth.

MI

Motivational Interviewing

A collaborative approach that helps you explore ambivalence, clarify values, and strengthen motivation for change.

PP

Positive Psychology

Builds on strengths, meaning, gratitude, resilience, and well-being alongside work on problems or symptoms.

TF

TF-CBT

Trauma-Focused Cognitive Behavioral Therapy

Uses trauma-sensitive CBT tools to help children, teens, and families process traumatic experiences safely.

BS

Brainspotting

Uses eye position and focused attention to help access and process distress, trauma, and emotional blocks.

PT

Play Therapy

Uses play, creativity, and developmentally appropriate tools to help children express feelings and build coping skills.

GT

Gestalt Therapy

Focuses on present-moment awareness, personal responsibility, and integrating thoughts, feelings, and actions.

BM

Behavior Modification

Uses practical strategies and reinforcement to build helpful behaviors and reduce patterns that are getting in the way.

FB

Faith-Based Counseling

Integrates a client's faith, values, and spiritual resources into therapy when that support feels important to them.

Therapy is not one-size-fits-all. Your therapist will work with you to find the approach, or blend of approaches, that fits you best.

Virginia Inge Gordon

LPC

Counseling for children, adolescents, adults, and couples, with special commitment to young people and caregivers.

EducationMS, Clinical Mental Health Counseling
Experience10+ years of clinical experience
About Virginia

Meaningful growth with service at the center.

Virginia is a Licensed Professional Counselor who has worked with clients experiencing depression, anxiety, relationship issues, parenting concerns, self-esteem concerns, grief, physical trauma, emotional abuse, and sexual abuse.

"To Live is To Serve." Frances Hesselbein

Education and early community work

In 2010, Virginia earned her bachelor's degree from the University of Alabama with a major in Psychology and a minor in Anthropology. Her commitment to serving adolescents began during college in 2008 when she served as a teaching assistant for Psychology 450, planning civic youth engagement events with at-risk high school students.

During the summer of 2009 in San Pedro Sula, Honduras, Virginia completed an independent study as primary investigator on self-esteem and family moral-religious emphasis among female adolescent Honduran orphans. Her research was published as a poster and presented at the 2010 Southeastern Psychological Association convention in Chattanooga.

Following college, Virginia volunteered at a Southeast Asian nonprofit in Bayou La Batre, Alabama, where she founded a youth empowerment program for middle and upper school students from 2010 to 2012. With support from administrators at Boat People SOS, she wrote a grant that created a paid role and facilitated teenage leadership groups. Their projects included park beautification with City Council approval, a bullying prevention campaign supported by Mobile District Attorney Ashley Rich, and a community carnival intended to lift morale following natural disasters including Hurricane Katrina. Virginia treasures receiving the name "Ai Vi" and the honor of being recognized as a Vietnamese American Leader after a year of training through the BPSOS 500 in 5 Years Pilot Project.

Clinical and public behavioral health experience

Virginia earned her master's degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from the University of Alabama at Birmingham in 2014. She has worked in adolescent residential, outpatient, school-based, and private practice settings, serving children, adolescents, adults, and couples. She has also witnessed the meaningful progress clients can make through virtual video-based therapy since the onset of COVID-19.

In 2016, Virginia helped develop the Eagle Rock Boys Ranch Mentoring Program in Etowah County, matching professional adult volunteers with at-risk youth needing support. The program, later known as APEX, continued to serve boys and adult mentors as of 2023.

While serving for more than two years as Clinical Behavioral Health Administrator at the Mobile County Health Department from 2018 to 2020, Virginia helped create and host more than 42 videos for the Wellness Wednesday with Virginia series. She also revised the health department's suicide policy in partnership with the psychology department at the University of South Alabama, developed practical suicide-prevention resources for primary care providers within their electronic medical record, delivered face-to-face training for more than 500 staff members, and developed suicide prevention video tutorials for staff.

During the onset of COVID-19, Virginia addressed the Mobile community virtually with behavioral health guidance for navigating the pandemic; her messages were broadcast by local news sources including Fox 10 News. In 2020, she also led a public forum with leaders from varied ethnic communities to address civil unrest in the nation.

What therapy is like with Virginia

Virginia primarily uses Motivational Interviewing, positive psychology, and Cognitive Behavioral Therapy to guide clients toward meaningful growth. She values a trusting therapeutic alliance and recognizes the importance of communication with caregivers when supporting young people.

Who Virginia works with

  • Children & adolescents
  • Adults
  • Couples
  • Depression
  • Anxiety
  • Parenting
  • Grief
  • Trauma & abuse recovery
  • Self-esteem
  • Infertility support

Service and professional affiliations

Virginia's service roles include Lifelines Rape Victim Advocate, Assistant Scout Master of Boy Scout Troop 505, and Father/Daughter Mentor and Coach for Outback of America.

She is a member of the American Counseling Association and the Alabama Counseling Association and a former board member of the Mobile Area Council, Boy Scouts of America. Virginia is also recognized by the American Society for Reproductive Medicine as a certified mental health professional providing care to infertility patients.

Media and resources

In 2022, Virginia collaborated with a former colleague from the Mobile County Health Department to launch TeenPOD on Spotify and Apple platforms. Through conversations with successful leaders and mentors, the podcast explores how people overcame adversity during their teen years. Her TeenPOD website serves as an additional hub of resources for teens and caregivers.
